name: Adaptive Audience Display – Elementor Conditional & Dynamic Visibility by Login & Role
author: Scott Mollett

sections.description:
Adaptive Audience Display adds login-based visibility controls to Elementor widgets, containers, and sections. It allows you to dynamically show or hide content based on whether the user is logged in or logged out.
Upgrade to Pro for advanced role-based visibility and premium features:
https://AdaptiveAudienceDisplay.com

Features

  • Visibility toggle for Elementor widgets, containers, and sections
  • Frontend enforcement after page republish
  • Lightweight and easy to use
  • Popup-based instructions page in admin
  • Compatible with Elementor’s rendering pipeline

Upgrade to Pro

Upgrade to Pro for advanced features including:
* Role-based visibility control for most elements within Elementor.
* Advanced diagnostics.
https://AdaptiveAudienceDisplay.com

Disclaimer

This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Elementor.
sections.installation:
1. Install via the WordPress plugin installer and Activate the plugin.
  2. Edit any Elementor widget, container, or section.
  3. Locate the “Adaptive Audience Display” panel in the Advanced tab.
  4. Choose visibility settings based on login state.
  5. Update and republish the page.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin support role-based visibility?

Yes, role-based visibility is supported in the PRO version. You can show or hide Elementor elements based on specific WordPress user roles.

Can I hide or show elements based on login status?

Yes, both the free and PRO versions allow you to control visibility based on whether the user is logged in or logged out.

Does it work with Elementor containers, sections, and widgets?

Yes, visibility logic applies to all Elementor elements including widgets, containers, and sections.

Do I need to republish the page for changes to apply?

Yes, after adjusting visibility settings, you need to update or republish the page for changes to take effect.

Is this plugin compatible with Elementor Pro?

Yes, it works with both Elementor Free and Elementor Pro.

Does it affect page speed or performance?

No, the plugin is lightweight and optimized for performance. Visibility logic runs only when necessary.

Can I use this with caching plugins?

Yes, but you may need to clear cache after making visibility changes to ensure they apply correctly.
